newsitem.title: USA: Coronado sees EPS rising next three years.
newsitem.headline: Coronado sees EPS rising next three years.

text.p: Coronado Industries Inc Wednesday said it expects earnings to rise in the next three years to $6.24 a share in 1999 from an estimated $2.36 a share in 1998 and $0.63 a share in 1997 as a result of the company's decision to begin manufacturing and marketing its patented, non-invasive treatment for open angle glaucoma.
In a statement, the company said net sales are expected to rise to $122.8 million in 1999 from an estimated $13.4 million in 1997.
In clinical trials conducted over the past three years, the treatment was found to have no harmful side effects like those associated with eye drops currently used to treat glaucoma, Coronado said.

Coronado estimates the potential world wide market for machine sales to be in excess of 100,000 machines. For every 100 machines sold the company will net approximately $1 million in profit per year from sales of their patented disposable suction rings.
Glaucoma is caused by a build up of pressure resulting in progressive damage to the optic nerve due to increased pressure within the eyeball. Over time, the result is a loss of vision.

The company said its "Vacuum Fixation Device and patented design suction ring" temporarily reduce Intra Ocular Pressure in the treatment of open angle glaucoma through a non-invasive treatment, the results of which last for an average of three months, at which time the treatment can be repeated with no serious side effects.
